title: EDGE-003-edgeball-lab-official-rules-draft
universal_lens: The EdgeBall Lab formalizes a constrained optimization over a state space of contest configurations, imposing strict boundary conditions that nullify financial and privacy vectors. By projecting the high-dimensional growth-os-v2 manifold onto a zero-cash, synthetic-data subspace, we isolate the pure structural dynamics of competitive engagement without regulatory singularities.
gsi_mapping: Within GSI, this draft establishes a conformal prediction framework where all input features are strictly synthetic. The Bayesian prior is heavily regularized to enforce zero-probability on real-money entry or live sportsbook affiliate flows, ensuring that any inferred user behavior remains entirely within the bounds of a safe, simulated sandbox.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the rulebook dictates a deterministic state-transition system. The engine continuously validates the current branch and dirty state against a P0 invariant: if any node in the decision tree implies a deposit, payout, or unauthorized data import, the feature flag automatically collapses the state to a disabled rollback configuration.

primitives.name: Zero-Cash Regulatory Invariant Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Do not launch paid contests, prizes, deposits, payouts, live leaderboards, sportsbook/DFS affiliate flows, or real-money entries without founder/legal approval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: C(t): Financial transaction volume (USD), dimensionless boolean for active status; A_Legal: Authorization matrix (Boolean).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a closed system where all monetary flows must be explicitly authorized by an external legal vector.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if C(t) > 0 without A_Legal = True, triggering immediate system halt.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE's compliance layer, acting as a hard constraint on the reward function of any deployed agent.
layer2.telemetry: Audit logs verifying zero outbound/inbound monetary transactions.

primitives.name: Synthetic Data Projection Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Do not import real friend-history data without explicit consent and deletion controls.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D_real: Real-world social graph data (Bytes); D_syn: Synthetic mock data (Bytes); Consent: Binary authorization flag.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes D_real is inherently hazardous and must be projected entirely into D_syn unless strict consent constraints are met.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if D_real enters the system without Consent = True, violating privacy boundaries.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's conformal inference masking, ensuring all training and inference datasets remain purely artificial.
layer2.telemetry: Data lineage tracking confirming 100% synthetic origin of contest inputs.

primitives.name: Feature Flag Rollback Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Feature flag disabled by default if code is ever approved.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F_flag: System activation state (Boolean); S_default: Default state = False.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a fail-safe architecture where the absence of explicit activation guarantees safety.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if F_flag defaults to True upon deployment, bypassing the safety gate.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSE's situational state machine, enforcing a 'disabled-by-default' transition policy.
layer2.telemetry: Deployment logs showing F_flag initialization status.

The EDGE-003 primitive set constructs a rigorous mathematical boundary around the EdgeBall Lab environment. We begin by defining the state space \Omega as the set of all possible contest configurations derived from growth-os-v2. The primary operator, Zero-Cash Invariant, acts as a projection matrix P_{0} that annihilates any vector component associated with financial transactions (deposits, payouts, affiliate flows). This ensures the resulting subspace \Omega' contains only non-monetary interactions. Simultaneously, the Synthetic Data Projection Kernel applies a transformation T_{syn} to the input data manifold, mapping any potential real-world social graph D_{real} to a purely synthetic counterpart D_{syn}, conditioned on a strict consent variable C=0. This dual projection isolates the core gameplay mechanics from regulatory and privacy risks. The Feature Flag Rollback Mechanism introduces a temporal control parameter \tau, where the system state S(\tau) is initialized to 'disabled'. Any attempt to transition to an 'active' state requires explicit, verified overrides, otherwise the system reverts to a safe baseline via a rollback operator R. The interplay of these operators creates a robust, self-correcting system where any deviation toward real-money gaming or unauthorized data usage triggers an immediate collapse back to the safe subspace. This mathematical formulation guarantees that the EdgeBall Lab remains a sterile testing ground, preserving the integrity of the underlying algorithms while completely neutralizing external liabilities.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits its structural rigor from early 20th-century operational calculus and modern regulatory technology (RegTech) constraints. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the opposing agents—namely, opportunistic developers or malicious actors—as utility maximizers seeking to exploit the system for financial gain or data exfiltration. Their decision-making process involves probing the boundary conditions of the contest design to find leakage points. However, our primitives anticipate this adversarial mindset by establishing hard, non-negotiable invariants. The agents quickly learn that any strategy involving real-money injection or unauthorized data access yields an immediate penalty (system halt), forcing them to operate strictly within the synthetic, zero-cash domain.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by ensuring that the financial, data, and execution layers operate on orthogonal axes. A veto condition is triggered if any correlation is detected between a feature flag activation and an unapproved data import or monetary flow. Specifically, if the gradient of the system state with respect to risk factors exceeds a predefined threshold, the cross-layer veto mechanism engages, instantly disabling the feature flag and initiating a rollback. This prevents any single point of failure from compromising the entire safety architecture.
